newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian court award Kragujevac TV to Zajedno.
newsitem.headline: Serbian court award Kragujevac TV to Zajedno.

text.p: Serbia's pro-democracy movement got a boost on Tuesday when a court awarded the local radio and television station in the town of Kragujevac to its opposition-ruled city council, station director said on Tuesday.

"The court reached a verdict on Monday which is favourable to us. We have already started broadcasting our radio programmes without any problems this morning while our television programme is due to go on air on Wednesday," Vidosav Stevanovic told Reuters.

The opposition Zajedno (Together) has won at the disputed local elections on November 17. Unlike events in the 14 biggest Serbian cities, Zajedno's victory in Kragujevac was not contested by the ruling leftist alliance.

But the ruling socialists wrest control over the local electronic media (RTK) by intergrating it last month into the state-run Serbian radio television network and moved police into the buildings to prevent Zajedno leaders from taking over.

The move provoked a siege of RTK buildings by Zajedno supporters and a bloody showdown with the police. The two sides compromised to ease tensions by leaving it to the court to decide on RTK's ownership.

"The court's decision is now effective and final. The authorities can prevent us from taking control over the station only by sending the police again but I do not expect such blatant violence," Stevanovic said.
